title: Zangsiwei prevents particulate matter-induced lung inflammation and fibrosis by inhibiting the TGF-beta/SMAD pathway.
authors: Wu, Zhijian; Song, Boyang; Peng, Fei; Zhang, Quan; Wu, Shangjie
one_liner_zh: 该文研究藏药ZSW通过TGF-beta/SMAD通路抑制颗粒物诱导的肺部炎症和纤维化，核心是药物机制与疾病表型，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，且分子对接仅用于药物-靶点预测，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Zangsiwei(ZSW) is a traditional Tibetan medicine from China consisting of extracts of Rhododendron anthopogonoides Maxim, Gentiana Tourn, Corydalis hendersonii Hemsl and Berberis kansuensis C.K.Schneid. Traditionally, ZSW has been used by Tibetan physicians to treat chronic respiratory diseases. The role of ZSW in particulate matter-induced lung inflammation and fibrosis remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: Combining non-targeted metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking to explore the mechanism of ZSW in the treatment of particulate matter-induced lung inflammation and fibrosis, and validated by in vivo and in vitro experiments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The serum metabolite profile post-ZSW administration was first identified utilizing non-targeted metabolomics. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were employed to predict potential bioactive components and their corresponding targets. The in silico predictions were subsequently validated through in vivo studies in mice exposed to PM2.5 and silica dust, as well as in vitro studies utilizing human lung epithelial cells (A549) and lung fibroblasts (MRC5). RESULTS: Metabolomic analysis identified specific serum metabolites that were associated with ZSW treatment. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified key targets involved in the Transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta)/SMAD pathway, which were subsequently validated through in vivo experiments demonstrating a reduction in lung inflammation and fibrosis in ZSW-treated mice. In vitro studies demonstrated that ZSW exerts protective effects against PM2.5-induced cytotoxicity and modulates fibrotic markers in a dose-dependent manner. This is consistent with the inhibition of the TGF-beta/SMAD pathway. CONCLUSION: Our integrated approach, which combines non-targeted metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking, followed by rigorous in vivo and in vitro validation, establishes ZSW as a potential therapeutic agent for particulate matter-induced lung inflammation and fibrosis.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：藏四味（ZSW）是一种源自中国的传统藏药，由烈香杜鹃（Rhododendron anthopogonoides Maxim）、龙胆（Gentiana Tourn）、齿叶玄参（Corydalis hendersonii Hemsl）和甘肃小檗（Berberis kansuensis C.K.Schneid）的提取物组成。传统上，ZSW被藏医用于治疗慢性呼吸系统疾病。ZSW在颗粒物诱导的肺部炎症和纤维化中的作用尚不清楚。研究目的：结合非靶向代谢组学、网络药理学和分子对接，探讨ZSW治疗颗粒物诱导的肺部炎症和纤维化的机制，并通过体内和体外实验进行验证。材料与方法：首先利用非靶向代谢组学鉴定ZSW给药后的血清代谢物谱。采用网络药理学和分子对接预测潜在生物活性成分及其相应靶点。随后，通过暴露于PM2.5和硅尘的小鼠体内研究，以及利用人肺上皮细胞（A549）和肺成纤维细胞（MRC5）的体外研究，验证了计算机模拟预测。结果：代谢组学分析鉴定了与ZSW治疗相关的特定血清代谢物。网络药理学和分子对接确定了参与转化生长因子-β（TGF-beta）/SMAD通路的关键靶点，并通过体内实验验证，显示ZSW处理的小鼠肺部炎症和纤维化减少。体外研究表明，ZSW对PM2.5诱导的细胞毒性具有保护作用，并以剂量依赖性方式调节纤维化标志物。这与TGF-beta/SMAD通路的抑制一致。结论：我们的综合方法结合了非靶向代谢组学、网络药理学和分子对接，随后进行了严格的体内和体外验证，确立了ZSW作为颗粒物诱导的肺部炎症和纤维化的潜在治疗药物。
